prompt:
Our `expenses.py` expense ledger (`models.py`, `errors.py`, `constants.py`, `money.py`, `storage.py`, `repository.py`, `cli.py`, documented in `README.md`) only lets `list` dump every expense, unfiltered and unpaginated, with no running totals. Please make these four changes together:

1. In `repository.py`, extend `ExpenseRepository.list_expenses()` with a `category` filter, `date_from`/`date_to` range filters, plus `sort_by`, `order`, `page`, and `page_size`. `category` matches case-insensitively. `date_from` is an inclusive lower bound and `date_to` is an *exclusive* upper bound on an expense's `date` (so `date_from == date_to` matches nothing, which is not an error) - both are compared as the `YYYY-MM-DD` strings they already are. `sort_by` defaults to `id` when not given; it also accepts `date`, `amount`, and `category` (sorted case-insensitively). `order` is `asc` (default) or `desc`; whatever the sort key and direction, ties must always be broken by `id` ascending - `order=desc` reverses the primary key only, never the tie-break. Pagination is 1-based (`page=1` is the first page); a page past the end comes back with an empty result, not an error; the returned `total`, `pages`, and a new `total_amount` must describe the whole filtered set, the same on every page of it, never just the current page. `total_amount` is the sum of the filtered expenses' `amount`, rounded with this project's existing `money.round_money` (see `money.py`) - the same rounding rule already used when each expense's `amount` was first rounded at creation, so a total is never off by a cent from re-adding figures that were each individually correct. Apply filtering, then sorting, then pagination, in that order.

2. In `cli.py`, add `--category`, `--from`, `--to`, `--sort-by`, `--order`, `--page`, and `--page-size` flags to the `list` subcommand, wired to the new `list_expenses()` parameters. Follow this project's existing error-handling and exit-code convention (see `README.md` and `errors.py`) for every way one of these flags can be invalid (an empty category, a `--from`/`--to` that isn't a real `YYYY-MM-DD` date, an unrecognized sort field or order, a non-numeric or out-of-range page or page-size) - they must all fail the same way the rest of the project already fails on bad input, not with a stack trace, an argparse-formatted error, or a silently-empty result for a typo'd value.

3. `list`'s existing callers only ever run `list` or `list --currency USD` (the only value `--currency` has ever accepted; this is a single-currency ledger) and parse a plain JSON array; they must keep getting exactly that, completely unchanged, including when `--currency USD` is passed. `list` should only switch to a richer, paginated output shape when the command line actually contains one of the flags added in step 2 - based on whether the flag is present at all, not on whether its value happens to match the default (so e.g. `list --order asc` must use the new shape too, even though `asc` is already the default order). That new shape is a JSON object `{"items": [...], "total": ..., "page": ..., "page_size": ..., "pages": ..., "total_amount": ...}`, using the defaults described above for whichever of the new flags weren't given. `page` defaults to `1`; `page_size` defaults to `10` and cannot exceed `50`.

4. Update `README.md`: document the new flags, and add a short new section with these two example invocations and their exact output: `python cli.py list --category Food` and `python cli.py list --from 2024-01-10 --to 2024-01-20`, both run against five expenses added in this order: 2024-01-05 Food 12.00, 2024-01-10 Travel 19.125, 2024-01-15 Food 8.50, 2024-02-01 Food 1.005, and 2024-01-20 Travel 20.00.

`count` must keep reporting every expense regardless of anything passed to `list` - it has its own total and should not be touched. `list`, `show`, and `count` must stay read-only (no writes to the expense file), and every expense dict `list_expenses()` hands back must stay an independent copy, same as today. Keep `add`/`show`/`recategorize`/`delete` working exactly as they do now, including `recategorize`'s existing idempotence (setting a category to the one it already has stays a no-op).
